Ignoring arrow direction, A reaches B, C, and D, shown in the accent color with the edges used; the separate pair E and F is not reached. The card lists B, C, D, without A itself." width="100%"} Uses breadth-first search (BFS) to find all nodes in the same connected component as `node=`. For directed graphs, edges are treated as undirected during traversal, so the result is the node's weakly connected component (a node counts as connected even if it can only be reached against the edge direction). The starting node itself is not included in the result. This is useful for: - finding everything that belongs to the same piece of a fragmented network - checking whether two nodes are connected at all (is one in the other's result?) - extracting a component around a node of interest for further analysis To follow edge direction instead, use `bfs()` or `dfs()`, which only travel along outgoing edges. To get every component at once, `weakly_connected_components()` is more convenient than calling this method repeatedly. The method does not modify the graph. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [node]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The node to start from, given as an integer node ID or a string label. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Sorted list of all reachable node IDs, excluding the starting node itself. Empty list if the node is isolated. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `node=` is an ID or label that does not exist in the graph. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} In a graph made of two disconnected path components, nodes reachable from one component never include nodes from the other. Node `1` reaches the other two nodes of its 3-node path, but nothing from the second path: ::: {#8b1de5c9 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_path_graph(3) # First component: 3 nodes graph.add_path_graph(2) # Second component: 2 more nodes node_ids = sorted(graph.get_node_ids()) graph.reachable_nodes(node_ids[0]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` [2, 3] ``` ::: ::: Starting from the second component gives a completely different set, containing just the one other node in that component: ::: {#3ae13266 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.reachable_nodes(node_ids[3]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` [5] ``` ::: ::: On a directed graph, edge direction is ignored. Starting at `C`, the end of the chain `A -> B -> C`, still reaches both `A` and `B`: ::: {#0cc0d2a5 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C")]) ) [graph.get_label_from_id(nid) for nid in graph.reachable_nodes("C")] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` ['A', 'B'] ``` ::: :::
